rows.text: This is the Bracket 4 version of Sisay for one reason: it destroys everybody's lands. Living Plane turns every land on the table into a creature, and Elesh Norn gives your creatures +2/+2 while giving theirs -2/-2 — so their entire mana base dies and yours grows. Mass land denial is not legal below Bracket 4, and it is the whole point of the build. Everything else is a tutor chain that assembles those two cards.

rows.name: Living Plane
rows.text: all lands are 1/1 creatures. On its own it does nothing; it is half of a one-sided Armageddon.

rows.name: Elesh Norn, Grand Cenobite
rows.text: your other creatures get +2/+2 and theirs get -2/-2. With any land animation out, every land your opponents control is a 1/1 or 2/2 taking -2/-2 — it dies immediately, and yours become 3/3s.

rows.name: Nature's Revolt
rows.text: the second copy of the animation, at 2/2.

rows.name: Natural Affinity
rows.text: the INSTANT-speed version. Hold it with Elesh Norn already on the battlefield and wipe the table's mana at the end of somebody's turn, or in response to removal aimed at Norn.

rows.name: Kudo, King Among Bears
rows.text: sets other creatures to base 2/2, which turns on the same interaction and shrinks every fatty at the table on the way.
Be deliberate about this. It ends games and it is miserable to sit through. Deploy it when you can actually close, not on turn five for value.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep a mana dork and a tutor. Turn-one acceleration into a turn-two or three Sisay is what makes the lock arrive before anyone can set up.
Assemble the animation and Elesh Norn in the SAME turn where possible. Living Plane on its own telegraphs everything and invites the enchantment removal that ruins the plan.
Natural Affinity is the surprise version. With Elesh Norn already down, holding three mana means you can wipe the table's lands at instant speed — usually at the end of the turn before yours.
Sisay finds lands too. Do not forget the legendary lands in your own mana base; against a table with no pressure, fetching a utility land is often better than a threat.
